newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica AAT may get lion's share of Telkom tender.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica AAT may get lion's share of Telkom tender.

text.p: Franco-South African firm Alcatel Altech Telecoms (AAT) said on Wednesday that it may get more than half of a giant two billion rand radio technology contract from telecommunications utility Telkom.
On Tuesday Telkom announced the tender award to ATT and U.S. firm Lucent Technologies Inc, but the exact split of the deal has not yet been decided.

"We don't imagine it will be any less than 50 percent for AAT and it could be more," said Bill Venter, chairman of Altron, the controlling shareholder in Allied Technologies Ltd (Altech) which owns 40 percent of AAT.
The two year contract is for the network planning, installation and supply of radio technology for 420,000 telephone lines in previously underserviced areas of South Africa.

AAT had to fight off international competition including the likes of Ericsson and Siemens to secure the order. Part of the deal is that most manufacturing will be local and both AAT and Lucent must seek to boost the use of black engineers and subcontractors.
AAT managing director John Pitout said seeking out and using black subcontractors could give work to 320 people, while expansion in other areas could see the creation of up to 90 more jobs.
In addition the 1,400 jobs at the firm's Boksburg manufacturing plant will now have long-term security.

About 18 million rand has already been spent on expanding the Boksburg plant's manufacturing capacity and AAT expects to spend about 100 million rand in total on the whole group to cope with the new business.
Venter declined to say how much AAT was hoping to make from the deal or the margins on which it had drawn up its bid.
He said revealing such information would hurt the competitive edge of the firm in current bids for another large Telkom contract and two other tenders in other African countries.
AAT's other shareholders are France's Alcatel, with 40 percent, and black investment group Rethabile with 20 percent.

Rethabile bought its AAT stake for 125 million rand earlier this year and group chief executive Moss Ngwenya said it would allow the firm to pay off its debts earlier as winning the Telkom contract had not been factored into its original projections.
Altech chief executive Craig Venter said Rethabile had played a key role in securing the deal and allowing AAT to come up with the black empowerment part of the bid.
"Rethabile's role in this tender was quite significant. They played a big role," he said.
